messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 - Single-cell epidemiology methods
messages.subject_clean: Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 - Single-cell epidemiology methods
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Cell-level evidence can add resolution to population health questions. Single Cell Data Analysis 2.0 led by Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Process single-cell RNA sequencing data through quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and differential expression analysis. Use R and Python tools, including Seurat and Scanpy, to integrate datasets and investigate cellular heterogeneity in epidemiological research. Connect computational results to biological inference while accounting for batch effects and data structure.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/single-cell-data-analysis-20-1
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Longitudinal Biostatistics Methods in R
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

Repeated observations require attention to correlation, missingness, and clustered study structures. Longitudinal Analysis in Biostatistics led by Md Tuhin Sheikh (Biostatistics, College of Health Solutions, Arizona State University) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Marginal and conditional models, correlation structures, and multilevel methods support analysis of repeated epidemiological observations. Participants use R and RStudio to address missingness patterns, multiple imputation, sensitivity analysis, and fixed and random effects. Epidemiologists can apply these approaches to cohort, patient, and clustered data when estimating change over time.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/longitudinal-analysis-in-biostatistics
The full course outline is available on the Instats course page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
